note: `Include F` does not copy F.f: it makes Challenge.f a delta alias whose CANONICAL name is Challenge.F.f. Environ.lookup_constant is keyed by the USER name, so a naive closure check looks Challenge.f up, finds F.f's declaration and compares the wrong kernel object. Here the target's own statement mentions f, and terms compare constants by canonical name, so the statement comparison rejects it first (observed: statement_mismatch / 'foo: the solution's statement differs from the challenge's'). The canonical-name check added alongside it is what catches the cases the statement comparison cannot see: the alias being the target itself (see module_include_admitted) or a closure member the statement does not mention directly.
